title: Omitting max_records_per_query buys 500 records per search, not a small sample
summary: The estimate is a deliberate UPPER bound built from the caps the request will actually send the provider. When `limits.max_records_per_query` is omitted it falls back to BULK_DEFAULT_RECORDS_PER_QUERY (500) — chosen to match what the Outscraper adapter really sends, so an omitted limit cannot make the estimate look optimistic. The consequence is that a body which reads as small (2 queries x 3 cities = 6 searches) is a 3,000-record purchase. Agents anchor on the search count because that is the number they wrote; the number that matters is records, and it is 500x larger by default.
